sanskrit: etat samīkṣyātmani cāvamānaṃ; niyamya manyuṃ balavān sa mānī rājānugaḥ saṃsadi kauravāṇāṃ; viniṣkraman vākyam uvāca bhīmaḥ
english: Perceiving this insult upon himself, the mighty and proud Bhīma, suppressing his rage, spoke these words as he departed from the assembly of the Kauravas in the king's retinue.

sanskrit: ahaṃ duryodhanaṃ hantā karṇaṃ hantā dhanaṃjayaḥ śakuniṃ cākṣakitavaṃ sahadevo haniṣyati
english: I shall slay Duryodhana; Dhanañjaya shall slay Karṇa; and Sahadeva shall slay Śakuni, that dice-cheat of Gāndhāra.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca bhūyo vakṣyāmi sabhāmadhye bṛhad vacaḥ satyaṃ devāḥ kariṣyanti yan no yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: And this further great vow I declare in the midst of the assembly — the gods shall make it true: there shall be war between us.

sanskrit: suyodhanam imaṃ pāpaṃ hantāsmi gadayā yudhi śiraḥ pādena cāsyāham adhiṣṭhāsyāmi bhūtale
english: I shall kill this sinful Suyodhana with my mace in battle, and I shall plant my foot upon his head on the ground.

sanskrit: vākyaśūrasya caivāsya paruṣasya durātmanaḥ duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ pātāsmi mṛgarāḍ iva
english: And the blood of this Duḥśāsana — this brave boaster of harsh words, this wicked soul — I shall drink like a lion.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca naiva vācā vyavasitaṃ bhīma vijñāyate satām itaś caturdaśe varṣe draṣṭāro yad bhaviṣyati
english: Arjuna said: O Bhīma, what is resolved by words is not recognized as the resolve of the righteous. In fourteen years from now, we shall see what comes to pass.

sanskrit: duryodhanasya karṇasya śakuneś ca durātmanaḥ duḥśāsanacaturthānāṃ bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
english: The earth shall drink the blood of Duryodhana, Karṇa, the wicked Śakuni, and Duḥśāsana as the fourth.

sanskrit: asūyitāraṃ vaktāraṃ prasraṣṭāraṃ durātmanām bhīmasena niyogāt te hantāhaṃ karṇam āhave
english: The slanderer, the speaker of insults, the releaser of the wicked — at your command, O Bhīmasena, I shall slay Karṇa in battle.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ pratijānīte bhīmasya priyakāmyayā karṇaṃ karṇānugāṃś caiva raṇe hantāsmi patribhiḥ
english: Arjuna vows, for the sake of Bhīma's satisfaction, that he shall slay Karṇa and those who follow Karṇa in battle with his arrows.

sanskrit: ye cānye pratiyotsyanti buddhimohena māṃ nṛpāḥ tāṃś ca sarvāñ śitair bāṇair netāsmi yamasādanam
english: And whatever other kings, deluded in their minds, shall fight against me — all of them I shall send to the abode of Yama with my sharp arrows.

sanskrit: caled dhi himavān sthānān niṣprabhaḥ syād divākaraḥ śaityaṃ somāt praṇaśyeta matsatyaṃ vicaled yadi
english: The Himālaya may move from its place, the sun may lose its splendor, the moon may lose its coolness — but my truth shall never waver.

sanskrit: na pradāsyati ced rājyam ito varṣe caturdaśe duryodhano hi satkṛtya satyam etad bhaviṣyati
english: If Duryodhana does not restore the kingdom after fourteen years from now, this sworn truth shall come to pass — mark it well.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktavati pārthe tu śrīmān mādravatīsutaḥ pragṛhya vipulaṃ bāhuṃ sahadevaḥ pratāpavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the son of Pṛthā had thus spoken, the glorious and valiant Sahadeva, son of Mādravatī, raising his mighty arm,

sanskrit: saubalasya vadhaṃ prepsur idaṃ vacanam abravīt krodhasaṃraktanayano niḥśvasann iva pannagaḥ
english: eager to slay the son of Subala, spoke these words with eyes red with rage, hissing like a serpent:

sanskrit: akṣān yān manyase mūḍha gāndhārāṇāṃ yaśohara naite 'kṣā niśitā bāṇās tvayaite samare vṛtāḥ
english: O fool, O destroyer of the glory of Gāndhāra! Those dice you think so highly of — know that these are not dice but sharpened arrows that you have chosen in battle.

sanskrit: yathā caivoktavān bhīmas tvām uddiśya sabāndhavam kartāhaṃ karmaṇas tasya kuru kāryāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: As Bhīma has already declared concerning you and your kinsmen, I shall perform that very deed. Do all that you need to do.

sanskrit: hantāsmi tarasā yuddhe tvāṃ vikramya sabāndhavam yadi sthāsyasi saṃgrāme kṣatradharmeṇa saubala
english: I shall swiftly slay you and your kinsmen in battle by my valor, if you stand firm in combat according to the dharma of the warrior class, O Saubala.

sanskrit: sahadevavacaḥ śrutvā nakulo 'pi viśāṃ pate darśanīyatamo nṝṇām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: O lord of the people, having heard Sahadeva's words, Nakula — the most handsome among men — also spoke these words:

sanskrit: suteyaṃ yajñasenasya dyūte 'smin dhṛtarāṣṭrajaiḥ yair vācaḥ śrāvitā rūkṣāḥ sthitair duryodhanapriye
english: This daughter of Yajñasena — at this dice match those who stood in favor of Duryodhana, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, caused her to hear such harsh words.

sanskrit: tān dhārtarāṣṭrān durvṛttān mumūrṣūn kālacoditān darśayiṣyāmi bhūyiṣṭham ahaṃ vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Those ill-conducted sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who seek their own death and are driven by fate — I shall show them in full measure the abode of Vivasvat's son, Yama.

sanskrit: nideśād dharmarājasya draupadyāḥ padavīṃ caran nirdhārtarāṣṭrāṃ pṛthivīṃ kartāsmi nacirād iva
english: Following the command of the king of dharma, and walking the path of Draupadī, I shall before long make this earth free of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: evaṃ te puruṣavyāghrāḥ sarve vyāyatabāhavaḥ pratijñā bahulāḥ kṛtvā dhṛtarāṣṭram upāgaman
english: Thus those tiger-men, all long-armed, having made many vows, approached Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āmantrayāmi bharatāṃs tathā vṛddhaṃ pitāmaham rājānaṃ somadattaṃ ca mahārājaṃ ca bāhlikam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I take leave of the Bharatas, and also of the aged grandfather Bhīṣma, of King Somadatta, and of the great king Bahlika.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ nṛpāṃś cānyān aśvatthāmānam eva ca viduraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca dhārtarāṣṭrāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: I take leave of Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the other kings, of Aśvatthāmā, of Vidura, of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and of all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: yuyutsuṃ saṃjayaṃ caiva tathaivānyān sabhāsadaḥ sarvān āmantrya gacchāmi draṣṭāsmi punar etya vaḥ
english: Taking leave of Yuyutsu, Sañjaya, and likewise all the other members of the assembly, I depart. I shall see you all again upon my return.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca na ca kiṃ cit tadocus te hriyā santo yudhiṣṭhiram manobhir eva kalyāṇaṃ dadhyus te tasya dhīmataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Overcome with shame, they said nothing at all to Yudhiṣṭhira. Only in their minds did those righteous ones wish well to that wise king.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca āryā pṛthā rājaputrī nāraṇyaṃ gantum arhati sukumārī ca vṛddhā ca nityaṃ caiva sukhocitā
english: Vidura said: The noble Pṛthā, princess by birth, ought not to go to the forest. She is delicate, old, and always accustomed to ease and comfort.

sanskrit: iha vatsyati kalyāṇī satkṛtā mama veśmani iti pārthā vijānīdhvam agadaṃ vo 'stu sarvaśaḥ
english: This auspicious lady shall dwell here, well honored in my house. Know this, O sons of Pṛthā. May you all be free from disease.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira vijānīhi mamedaṃ bharatarṣabha nādharmeṇa jitaḥ kaś cid vyathate vai parājayāt
english: Know this word of mine, O Yudhiṣṭhira, O bull among Bharatas: no one who has been defeated by adharma is truly afflicted by defeat.

sanskrit: tvaṃ vai dharmān vijānīṣe yudhāṃ vettā dhanaṃjayaḥ hantārīṇāṃ bhīmaseno nakulas tv arthasaṃgrahī
english: You are the knower of dharma; Dhanañjaya is the knower of battle; Bhīmasena is the slayer of enemies; Nakula is the gatherer of resources.

sanskrit: saṃyantā sahadevas tu dhaumyo brahmaviduttamaḥ dharmārthakuśalā caiva draupadī dharmacāriṇī
english: Sahadeva is the controller; Dhaumya is the foremost knower of Brahman; and Draupadī is skilled in dharma and artha, a woman who walks the path of dharma.

sanskrit: anyonyasya priyāḥ sarve tathaiva priyavādinaḥ parair abhedyāḥ saṃtuṣṭāḥ ko vo na spṛhayed iha
english: You are all dear to one another, and likewise speak kindly to one another; you are unbreakable by enemies and content. Who among men here would not envy you?

sanskrit: eṣa vai sarvakalyāṇaḥ samādhis tava bhārata nainaṃ śatrur viṣahate śakreṇāpi samo 'cyuta
english: This, O Bharata, is the all-auspicious resolution that you have — no enemy can withstand it, even one equal to Śakra himself. Be steadfast.

sanskrit: himavaty anuśiṣṭo 'si merusāvarṇinā purā dvaipāyanena kṛṣṇena nagare vāraṇāvate
english: You were instructed long ago on the Himālayas by Meru-Savarni, and by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana in the city of Vāraṇāvata.

sanskrit: bhṛgutuṅge ca rāmeṇa dṛṣadvatyāṃ ca śaṃbhunā aśrauṣīr asitasyāpi maharṣer añjanaṃ prati
english: By Rāma on the peak of Bhṛgutuṅga, and by Shambhu on the banks of the Dṛṣadvatī — you have also heard the teachings of the great sage Asita concerning Mount Añjana.

sanskrit: draṣṭā sadā nāradasya dhaumyas te 'yaṃ purohitaḥ mā hārṣīḥ sāṃparāye tvaṃ buddhiṃ tām ṛṣipūjitām
english: Your priest Dhaumya is ever a beholder of Nārada's wisdom. Do not in adversity lose that understanding which the sages have honored.

sanskrit: purūravasam ailaṃ tvaṃ buddhyā jayasi pāṇḍava śaktyā jayasi rājño 'nyān ṛṣīn dharmopasevayā
english: O Pāṇḍava, you surpass Purūravas son of Ila in wisdom; you surpass other kings in power; and you surpass the sages in your devotion to dharma.

sanskrit: aindre jaye dhṛtamanā yāmye kopavidhāraṇe visarge caiva kaubere vāruṇe caiva saṃyame
english: In Indra's sphere — steadfastness toward victory; in Yama's — restraint of wrath; in Kubera's — generosity; in Varuṇa's — self-control.

sanskrit: ātmapradānaṃ saumyatvam adbhyaś caivopajīvanam bhūmeḥ kṣamā ca tejaś ca samagraṃ sūryamaṇḍalāt
english: Self-giving and gentleness come from Soma; sustenance of life from the waters; forbearance from the earth; and full radiance from the orb of the sun.

sanskrit: vāyor balaṃ viddhi sa tvaṃ bhūtebhyaś cātmasaṃbhavam agadaṃ vo 'stu bhadraṃ vo drakṣyāmi punarāgatān
english: Know that strength comes from Vāyu and that the self is born from the elements. May you all be free from affliction, may good be yours — I shall see you upon your return.

sanskrit: āpaddharmārthakṛcchreṣu sarvakāryeṣu vā punaḥ yathāvat pratipadyethāḥ kāle kāle yudhiṣṭhira
english: In crises of duty, purpose, and hardship, and in all affairs whatsoever, act rightly and in accordance with the time, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: āpṛṣṭo 'sīha kaunteya svasti prāpnuhi bhārata kṛtārthaṃ svastimantaṃ tvāṃ drakṣyāmaḥ punarāgatam
english: You are bidden farewell here, O son of Kuntī. May you fare well, O Bharata. We shall see you again when you return, your purpose accomplished and in safety.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tathety uktvā pāṇḍavaḥ satyavikramaḥ bhīṣmadroṇau namaskṛtya prātiṣṭhata yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, that Pāṇḍava of true valor said "So be it," and Yudhiṣṭhira, bowing to Bhīṣma and Droṇa, set forth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin saṃprasthite kṛṣṇā pṛthāṃ prāpya yaśasvinīm āpṛcchad bhṛśaduḥkhārtā yāś cānyās tatra yoṣitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When he had set forth, Kṛṣṇā — Draupadī — deeply afflicted with grief, went to the glorious Pṛthā and took leave of her, as did the other women present there.

sanskrit: yathārhaṃ vandanāśleṣān kṛtvā gantum iyeṣa sā tato ninādaḥ sumahān pāṇḍavāntaḥpure 'bhavat
english: Having duly offered salutations and embraces as was befitting, she desired to depart; then a great wailing arose in the inner quarters of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: kuntī ca bhṛśasaṃtaptā draupadīṃ prekṣya gacchatīm śokavihvalayā vācā kṛcchrād vacanam abravīt
english: And Kuntī, deeply tormented, seeing Draupadī departing, spoke with voice faltering in grief, with great difficulty:

sanskrit: vatse śoko na te kāryaḥ prāpyedaṃ vyasanaṃ mahat strīdharmāṇām abhijñāsi śīlācāravatī tathā
english: "Dear child, you must not grieve though this great calamity has befallen you. You know the dharma of women, and you are endowed with righteous conduct and behavior.

sanskrit: na tvāṃ saṃdeṣṭum arhāmi bhartṝn prati śucismite sādhvīguṇasamādhānair bhūṣitaṃ te kuladvayam
english: O pure-smiling one, I have no need to instruct you regarding your husbands. Both your lineages are adorned with the virtues of noble women.

sanskrit: sabhāgyāḥ kuravaś ceme ye na dagdhās tvayānaghe ariṣṭaṃ vraja panthānaṃ madanudhyānabṛṃhitā
english: Fortunate are these Kurus that they have not been consumed by you, O sinless one. Go along the auspicious path, sustained by my thoughts upon you.

sanskrit: bhāviny arthe hi satstrīṇāṃ vaiklavyaṃ nopajāyate gurudharmābhiguptā ca śreyaḥ kṣipram avāpsyasi
english: For good women, faintheartedness does not arise when great things are at stake. Protected by the dharma of your elders, you shall quickly attain what is best.

sanskrit: sahadevaś ca me putraḥ sadāvekṣyo vane vasan yathedaṃ vyasanaṃ prāpya nāsya sīden mahan manaḥ
english: And my son Sahadeva must be continually watched over while he dwells in the forest, so that when he encounters this adversity his noble mind does not sink."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu sā devī sravannetrajalāvilā śoṇitāktaikavasanā muktakeśy abhiniryayau
english: Saying "So be it," that goddess, her eyes streaming with tears, wearing a single blood-stained garment, with hair unbound, departed.

sanskrit: tāṃ krośantīṃ pṛthā duḥkhād anuvavrāja gacchatīm athāpaśyat sutān sarvān hṛtābharaṇavāsasaḥ
english: Pṛthā followed after her as she went, crying out in grief. Then she saw all her sons stripped of their ornaments and fine garments,

sanskrit: rurucarmāvṛtatanūn hriyā kiṃ cid avāṅmukhān paraiḥ parītān saṃhṛṣṭaiḥ suhṛdbhiś cānuśocitān
english: their bodies covered with deerskins and bark cloth, with faces slightly downcast in shame, surrounded by enemies rejoicing and lamented by their friends.

sanskrit: tadavasthān sutān sarvān upasṛtyātivatsalā sasvajānāvadac chokāt tat tad vilapatī bahu
english: That most affectionate mother, approaching all her sons in that condition, embraced them and cried out in grief, lamenting again and again in many ways.

sanskrit: kathaṃ saddharmacāritravṛttasthitivibhūṣitān akṣudrān dṛḍhabhaktāṃś ca daivatejyāparān sadā
english: "How have you — adorned with righteous conduct, behavior, and steadfastness; not small-minded; firm in devotion; and always engaged in reverence to the gods —

sanskrit: vyasanaṃ vaḥ samabhyāgāt ko 'yaṃ vidhiviparyayaḥ kasyāpadhyānajaṃ cedam āgaḥ paśyāmi vo dhiyā
english: come to meet with this calamity? What is this inversion of fate? By whose ill-thinking has this sin been born? I see it when I reflect with my understanding.

sanskrit: syāt tu madbhāgyadoṣo 'yaṃ yāhaṃ yuṣmān ajījanam duḥkhāyāsabhujo 'tyarthaṃ yuktān apy uttamair guṇaiḥ
english: Surely this is the fault of my own fate, that I gave birth to you — you who are endowed with the highest virtues yet bear an exceeding portion of pain and suffering.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vatsyatha durgeṣu vaneṣv ṛddhivinākṛtāḥ vīryasattvabalotsāhatejobhir akṛśāḥ kṛśāḥ
english: How shall you dwell in the difficult and harsh forests, stripped of your wealth — you who are not weak in valor, courage, strength, enterprise, and splendor — and yet made wretched?

sanskrit: yady etad aham ajñāsyaṃ vanavāso hi vo dhruvam śataśṛṅgān mṛte pāṇḍau nāgamiṣyaṃ gajāhvayam
english: If I had known that forest-exile was indeed certain for you, I would not have come to Hāstinapura from Shatashrunga after the death of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: dhanyaṃ vaḥ pitaraṃ manye tapomedhānvitaṃ tathā yaḥ putrādhim asaṃprāpya svargecchām akarot priyām
english: I consider your father fortunate — endowed with austerity and wisdom — who, before reaching the grief over sons, made his longing for heaven a cherished goal.

sanskrit: dhanyāṃ cātīndriyajñānām imāṃ prāptāṃ parāṃ gatim manye 'dya mādrīṃ dharmajñāṃ kalyāṇīṃ sarvathaiva hi
english: And I consider blessed in every way Mādrī — the knower of dharma, the auspicious one — who today has attained that supreme state beyond the senses.

sanskrit: ratyā matyā ca gatyā ca yayāham abhisaṃdhitā jīvitapriyatāṃ mahyaṃ dhig imāṃ kleśabhāginīm
english: Cursed is this fondness for life that was instilled in me through love, wisdom, and circumstance — I who am a sharer in suffering."

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatīṃ kuntīm abhisāntvya praṇamya ca pāṇḍavā vigatānandā vanāyaiva pravavrajuḥ
english: Consoling Kuntī as she lamented thus, and bowing to her, the Pāṇḍavas, bereft of joy, set forth for the forest.

sanskrit: vidurādayaś ca tām ārtāṃ kuntīm āśvāsya hetubhiḥ prāveśayan gṛhaṃ kṣattuḥ svayam ārtatarāḥ śanaiḥ
english: Vidura and the others, consoling the afflicted Kuntī with words of reason, led her into Vidura's house, themselves more grieved than she, moving slowly.

sanskrit: rājā ca dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ sa śokākulitacetanaḥ kṣattuḥ saṃpreṣayām āsa śīghram āgamyatām iti
english: And king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, his mind overwhelmed with sorrow, sent word to Vidura: "Come quickly."

sanskrit: tato jagāma viduro dhṛtarāṣṭraniveśanam taṃ paryapṛcchat saṃvigno dhṛtarāṣṭro narādhipaḥ
english: Then Vidura went to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's dwelling. The agitated king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, questioned him.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kathaṃ gacchati kaunteyo dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmasenaḥ savyasācī mādrīputrau ca tāv ubhau
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How does the son of Kuntī, King Yudhiṣṭhira the dharmaraja, go? And Bhīmasena, and the ambidextrous Arjuna, and those two sons of Mādrī?

sanskrit: dhaumyaś caiva kathaṃ kṣattar draupadī vā tapasvinī śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ sarvaṃ teṣām aṅgaviceṣṭitam
english: And how does Dhaumya go? And the suffering Draupadī? O Vidura, I wish to hear all about the movements of their limbs and bearing.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca vastreṇa saṃvṛtya mukhaṃ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bāhū viśālau kṛtvā tu bhīmo gacchati pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Vidura said: The son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, goes covering his face with his garment. And Bhīma the Pāṇḍava goes with his broad arms stretched wide.

sanskrit: sikatā vapan savyasācī rājānam anugacchati mādrīputraḥ sahadevo mukham ālipya gacchati
english: Savyasācī, the ambidextrous Arjuna, follows the king scattering sand. The son of Mādrī, Sahadeva, goes with his face smeared.

sanskrit: pāṃsūpaliptasarvāṅgo nakulaś cittavihvalaḥ darśanīyatamo loke rājānam anugacchati
english: Nakula, the most beautiful in the world, his entire body smeared with dust and his mind bewildered, follows the king.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇā keśaiḥ praticchādya mukham āyatalocanā darśanīyā prarudatī rājānam anugacchati
english: Kṛṣṇā, with long eyes, beautiful, weeping, her face covered by her hair, follows the king.

sanskrit: dhaumyo yāmyāni sāmāni raudrāṇi ca viśāṃ pate gāyan gacchati mārgeṣu kuśān ādāya pāṇinā
english: Dhaumya, O lord of the people, goes along the roads chanting the Sāman hymns of Yama and of Rudra, holding kusa grass in his hand.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca vividhānīha rūpāṇi kṛtvā gacchanti pāṇḍavāḥ tan mamācakṣva vidura kasmād evaṃ vrajanti te
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The Pāṇḍavas go in various forms and bearing. Explain this to me, O Vidura — why do they go in this manner?

sanskrit: vidura uvāca nikṛtasyāpi te putrair hṛte rājye dhaneṣu ca na dharmāc calate buddhir dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
english: Vidura said: Even though deceived by your sons, even though his kingdom and wealth have been taken, the mind of the wise Dharmarāja never wavers from dharma.

sanskrit: yo 'sau rājā ghṛṇī nityaṃ dhārtarāṣṭreṣu bhārata nikṛtyā krodhasaṃtapto nonmīlayati locane
english: That king, who is ever compassionate toward the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Bharata, inflamed with anger at the treachery done to him, does not open his eyes —

sanskrit: nāhaṃ janaṃ nirdaheyaṃ dṛṣṭvā ghoreṇa cakṣuṣā sa pidhāya mukhaṃ rājā tasmād gacchati pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "Lest I burn the people with my terrible gaze" — it is for this reason that the Pāṇḍava king covers his face and so departs.

sanskrit: yathā ca bhīmo vrajati tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu bāhvor bale nāsti samo mameti bharatarṣabha
english: And why Bhīma goes as he does — hear it from me as I describe it, O bull among Bharatas: "There is none equal to me in the strength of my arms" —

sanskrit: bāhū viśālau kṛtvā tu tena bhīmo 'pi gacchati bāhū darśayamāno hi bāhudraviṇadarpitaḥ cikīrṣan karma śatrubhyo bāhudravyānurūpataḥ
english: it is for this reason that Bhīma also goes with his broad arms stretched wide, displaying those arms — proud in the wealth of his arms, intending to perform deeds against his enemies befitting the treasure of those arms.
